brief.scope: Independently review C2 task output semantics against the owning contracts, frozen reviewed tests and producer record. Read current AGENTS.md and ops/README.md. Scope is envelope.py/outputs.py only; verify no frozen test/catalogue edits and compare all five supplied test hashes. Run test_job_outputs*.py and the full task suite where allowed. Check native declarations versus strict JSON decoding, closed shape, paths/reservations/collisions, exact rendering/handles, optional commit transport, legacy preservation and the narrow inline exception. Catalogue activation must remain deferred to canonical launcher consumption. Do not edit code/tests or create runtime authority. Return exact refs, approve/changes, findings, measured commands and limits in the inline envelope. This is library acceptance, not launch/live-capability approval.

findings.claim: Optional commit transport is reconciled on one side of task's own seam only. Declared: CONTRACT.md:129-135 names the reconciliation this change performs — "The optional write job `commit` transport also needs later reconciliation with the validator's fixed fields" — and gives its reproduction pointer as `sed -n '297,335p' ops/devlane/task/run.py`, which is _candidate_envelope/_parse_envelope. Practiced: envelope.py:434 now filters `commit` out of the key-order check so validate accepts the member ENVELOPE_SCHEMA has advertised since 710dbac (blob 1451eef line 100), while run.py:298 and run.py:306 still recognize an envelope by `tuple(value) == envelope.FIELDS`. Measured on one value: envelope.build produces an envelope, the schema-advertised commit member is added, envelope.validate returns it, and run._candidate_envelope and run._parse_envelope both return None for the identical dict and its JSON text, nested under 'result' as well; the same envelope minus commit is found. A worker that follows the schema task hands it therefore reads as "no envelope" on this path — an absence where an answer was held. This is not a regression: both seams refused commit before, so nothing that worked has stopped working, and envelope.py was the producer's only permitted file. It is the unpaid half of the named reconciliation, and it is now observable because the other half was paid.

The catalogue seam cannot carry transport reservations. Declared: CONTRACT.md:343-346 — "Launch supplies adapter/launcher transport reservations to validation; equal, ancestor or descendant collisions refuse… The list must include any further transport paths an adapter needs." Practiced: validate_outputs and load_outputs both take reserved=, but outputs_from_job(spec) — the seam a launcher reaches for once jobs.json is decoded — calls validate_outputs(spec.get("outputs", _OMITTED)) with no reserved passthrough, and render_declared_outputs/append_declared_outputs have no reserved parameter either. Measured: the array [{"kind":"file","path":"adapter-state.json","artifact":"state"}] refuses through validate_outputs(..., reserved=("adapter-state.json",)) and is admitted unchanged through outputs_from_job on a job spec carrying the same array. Reachable only at adoption, since nothing calls these seams yet; naming it now so the launcher integration does not inherit a validation entry point that silently drops the adapter's own reservations.

Duplicate JSON object members are refused only on a seam the catalogue will not use. Declared: CONTRACT.md:332-333 — "Task's semantic declaration validation additionally rejects duplicate JSON object members…" Practiced: that check lives in load_outputs' object_pairs hook, which takes JSON text for one outputs array. jobs.json is a whole catalogue and is decoded elsewhere with an ordinary json load, after which the repeated member has already collapsed; outputs_from_job then sees valid native data. Measured: load_outputs refuses the one-line duplicate-path fixture, and the same array reached through json.loads of a catalogue fragment is admitted as the collapsed last member, path "B.md". The frozen tests deliberately put this duty on the text seam and the reviewed ruling accepted that, so this is not a departure from the tests; it is the residual coverage question adoption must answer — either launch re-encodes the outputs member through load_outputs, or a catalogue-level strict decode is owed.

One of the three C2 refusal classes is not an OutputsError. Declared: envelope.py:122 introduces OutputsError as "A declaration or bound output path cannot satisfy C2", and dispatch/CONTRACT.md:294-303 names outputs-schema, outputs-path and outputs-handle as C2 refusal ids. Practiced: _outputs_refuse raises OutputsError for outputs-schema and outputs-path, while the handle mismatch at envelope.py:507 raises a bare EnvelopeError with an "outputs-handle:" prefix. Measured: the schema and path refusals are OutputsError instances; the handle refusal is an EnvelopeError that is not an OutputsError. Nothing breaks today because OutputsError subclasses EnvelopeError and every frozen test asserts the base, but a consumer that catches OutputsError to classify C2 refusals — the reason the subclass exists — silently misses the handle class.

Inertness. grep across ops/ and .claude/ for validate_outputs, load_outputs, outputs_from_job, render_declared_outputs, append_declared_outputs, OUTPUTS_SCHEMA, TRANSPORT_RESERVED, OutputsError and inline_planning_exception, excluding envelope.py and its tests, returns nothing. grep -c outputs ops/devlane/task/jobs.json is 0. Nothing calls the new seams and the catalogue declares nothing, so activation stays deferred to canonical launcher consumption and no runtime authority is created. Launch was not touched; its writable_out job-name branch is the same defect C1 recorded.

Against the contract, seam by seam. Native declarations versus strict decoding: outputs_from_job reads only an explicit outputs member, treats a missing key as omission and refuses an explicit null, never touching prompt prose or the job name — and validate_outputs' signature carries no job parameter, so authorization cannot branch on identity. load_outputs is the text seam and is strict in both directions the ruling asked for: an object_pairs hook that refuses a repeated member before dict collapse, and parse_constant refusing NaN/Infinity. Closed shape: exact member sets per kind, additionalProperties nowhere honoured by accident. Grammar: re.fullmatch, not re.match, so a trailing newline cannot slip past the anchor — the case the corrected test now pins. Paths, reservations, collisions: _overlaps compares segment-wise, reservations are unioned with the defaults so a supplied list can only tighten, and every reserved entry is itself checked against the path grammar. Rendering: the check-tests example reproduces byte for byte at /jobs/example/out; json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) gives lowercase hex and no optional slash escaping; declaration order is visit order; omission and [] both render the none-grant line; a bound path that cannot be a handle refuses outputs-path before anything is emitted. Exact handles: decoded string equality, so a dot-segment, trailing-slash or JSON-quoted spelling that would resolve to the same file refuses. Legacy preservation: validate(env) with no outputs keyword leaves historical relative and non-canonical handles valid, and out_root is only reached when a row exists. The narrow inline exception is gated on inline_planning_exception is True and job == 'plan' and, in the outputs loop, additionally on artifact 'plan' at path PLAN.md, so it does not reach a skeptic report or a ruling and is not an outputs kind.

Worth saying plainly: this change closes a real declared-versus-practiced gap rather than opening one. ENVELOPE_SCHEMA has advertised an optional commit object to structured-output harnesses since 710dbac while validate refused any envelope carrying it. That contradiction is gone. The P2 is that the same reconciliation stops at the module boundary — run.py still recognizes an envelope by exact key-tuple equality, so it drops the very envelope validate now accepts. CONTRACT.md:133-135 names that file and those lines as the reproduction for this work. envelope.py was the producer's only permitted file, so this is a follow-up obligation, not a reason to send the library back; it must be discharged before any launcher integration claims commit transport works end to end.

Opinion 1, not chargeable. With the flag on, artifacts['plan'] goes through _text, which accepts any non-empty string — including a wrong absolute handle. The flag disables the exact-handle check for that key rather than switching on the value's shape, so an inlined plan and a misdirected handle are indistinguishable while it is set. The contract does not specify a discriminator and the frozen test pins the accepting arm; the flag is launch-supplied and the exception is temporary. Worth defining when its transition is independently defined and tested, as the adoption checklist already requires.

Opinion 2, not chargeable. _outputs_refuse uses one fixed needed clause, "correct trusted output declaration or canonical output root", for both classes, so an outputs-path refusal still offers the declaration remedy and vice versa. Expected, found and needed are all present and found always names the offending value, which is what docs/wire.md demands; the remedy is merely wider than the failure.

Opinion 3, not chargeable. append_declared_outputs evaluates prompt.rstrip("\r\n") first, so a non-string prompt raises AttributeError rather than a refusal, and out_root is validated only when at least one row binds a path — an empty declaration renders the none-grant line against any root. Both inputs are trusted catalogue and launcher data, not worker data, and no contract row is left unpinned.

Firewall. I neither wrote nor approved these tests and did not produce the implementation; the tests were authored by Grok 4.6, corrected by the same author, and independently approved at 026fcad and 43cd8b5 by an earlier Opus 5 reviewer. I read the retained patch only as it landed in the tree. The dangling record pointers the final test review raised at 20260906T112240Z-tests-grok-6e070c are outside this scope and I did not re-measure them.

Freeze readiness: yes for the library. envelope.py implements what the frozen, independently reviewed tests demand, at 99/99 and 312/312, with every frozen artifact byte-identical and the catalogue untouched and inert. The four findings are for the adoption slice that consumes it.
